title: Automating a Shopify store from order to delivery
excerpt: What actually gets automated when an order lands, and where a human still needs to step in.
author: heba-hesham
body:
Most stores lose time in the gap between a paid order and a shipped parcel. The order arrives, someone copies it into a supplier sheet, someone else chases a tracking number, and the customer emails to ask where their parcel is. Shopify automation, including shipping automation, closes that gap: each step triggers the next one on its own, and your team only steps in when something actually needs a person.

This guide walks through what that chain looks like for a store in Egypt, which parts are worth automating first, and where a human should stay in the loop.

## Where the time goes between "paid" and "delivered"

If you run a Shopify store, the order itself is the easy part. Shopify takes the payment, sends a confirmation and adds the order to your dashboard. The work starts after that, and most of it happens outside Shopify:

- **Copying orders to suppliers.** Someone opens the order, writes the products and quantities into a spreadsheet or a WhatsApp message, and sends it to the supplier or the warehouse.
- **Booking the shipment.** Someone logs into the courier's portal, types the customer's name, address and phone number again, and books a pickup.
- **Chasing tracking numbers.** The courier sends a tracking number. Someone copies it back into Shopify so the customer can see it.
- **Answering "where is my order?"** Customers who don't get an update message you on WhatsApp or Instagram, and someone has to look the order up and reply.
- **Fixing mistakes.** A wrong address, a product that is out of stock, a parcel that comes back. Each one starts a new round of messages.

None of these tasks is hard. The problem is that they repeat for every single order, and every copy-and-paste is a chance for a typo. A store with 30 orders a day can easily spend several hours a day just moving information from one screen to another.

## What Shopify automation from order to delivery looks like

The fix is not one tool. It is a chain, where each step starts the next one automatically:

1. **The order is paid.** Shopify sends the order details the moment payment is confirmed (or the moment you confirm a cash-on-delivery order).
2. **The supplier is notified.** The order is routed to the right supplier or warehouse based on the products in it. If one order contains items from two suppliers, each one only receives their part.
3. **The supplier confirms.** When the supplier marks the order as ready, that confirmation is recorded against the order, with the time it happened.
4. **The shipment is created.** The customer's details are sent straight to the courier to [create a shipment](/systems/courier-system), so nobody types the address twice.
5. **The tracking number goes back to the customer.** The tracking number is written back into Shopify, and the customer gets a message on WhatsApp or by email with a link to follow the parcel.
6. **Stock is updated everywhere.** The sold quantity is deducted on every channel you sell on, so you don't sell a product you no longer have.
7. **Any break raises a flag.** If a step doesn't happen on time (the supplier hasn't confirmed, the courier rejected the address, a parcel is stuck), your team gets an alert with the whole order history attached.

Once it runs, the normal orders move from payment to delivery without anyone touching them. That is what our [order-to-delivery automation](/solutions/order-fulfillment) is built to do.

## Shopify shipping automation with couriers in Egypt

For stores in Egypt, the courier step is usually where most of the manual work sits, because each shipping company has its own portal and its own way of handling cash on delivery.

Many couriers that work with online stores in Egypt offer a way to create shipments directly from your store's data instead of typing them into their website. When that connection exists, the automation can:

- create the shipment with the right address, phone number and cash-on-delivery amount,
- receive the tracking number and the delivery status updates,
- tell the customer when the parcel is out for delivery, and
- flag returns and failed deliveries to your team the same day.

If your courier doesn't offer a direct connection, the chain can still prepare the shipment file in the exact format the courier needs, so the only manual step left is uploading it.

## What to automate first

You don't need to automate everything on day one. Start with the step that costs your team the most time or causes the most mistakes. For most stores, the order is:

1. **Tracking updates to customers.** This alone cuts most "where is my order?" messages, and it is quick to set up.
2. **Shipment creation with the courier.** This removes the biggest source of typing errors: addresses and phone numbers.
3. **Supplier routing.** If you work with several suppliers or a separate warehouse, sending each one only their part of the order saves a lot of back-and-forth.
4. **Stock sync across channels.** Important as soon as you sell on more than one channel, such as your Shopify store and Instagram.

Each step you add removes a manual task and keeps working while you sleep.

## Where a person should stay in the loop

Good automation doesn't remove people. It removes the repetitive parts so your team can focus on the orders that need judgment. Keep a person involved when:

- **An address looks incomplete or wrong.** The automation can flag it, but someone should call the customer before the parcel is booked.
- **A product is out of stock after the order was placed.** The customer should hear from a person, with an alternative or a refund.
- **A delivery fails or a parcel is returned.** Deciding whether to reship, refund or cancel is a business decision.
- **A customer is upset.** An automatic message is fine for "your order has shipped", not for a complaint.

The difference is that these cases now reach your team with everything attached: the order, the supplier's confirmation, the courier's status and every message sent to the customer. Nobody starts from zero.

## What changes for your store

When the chain is in place, a few things change quickly:

- **Fewer mistakes.** Data is entered once, at checkout, by the customer, and then moves on its own.
- **Faster shipping.** Orders reach the supplier and the courier minutes after payment, not when someone gets to them.
- **Fewer support messages.** Customers who get tracking updates don't need to ask.
- **Time back for your team.** The hours spent copying data go into selling, marketing and serving customers.

You can see how this worked for a real store in our case study of an [e-commerce store in Cairo](/case-studies/ecommerce-store-cairo), which moved from handling orders by hand to a fully automated flow in six weeks.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I automate my Shopify store if I use cash on delivery?

Yes. The chain starts when you confirm the order instead of when the payment arrives, and the cash-on-delivery amount is sent to the courier with the shipment. Delivery and collection status come back into the same order.

### Do I need to change my courier or my suppliers?

No. Shopify automation is built around the courier and suppliers you already work with. If a courier has no direct connection, we prepare the shipment file in the format they accept.

### How long does it take to set up?

It depends on how many suppliers, couriers and sales channels you have. Most stores start with tracking updates and shipment creation, then add the other steps once those run smoothly. We give you a clear timeline after a free audit of your store.

### What happens if something goes wrong in the middle of the chain?

The step that failed raises an alert to your team, with the full order history attached. The rest of your orders keep moving, and nothing is lost or sent twice.

---

title: What AI ad management actually does to your ROAS
excerpt: Budget reallocation, creative testing and the unglamorous parts that move return on ad spend.
author: heba-hesham
body:
The headline number is ROAS, but the work behind it is repetitive: check which ad sets earned their spend yesterday, move budget toward them, pause what is dragging, and keep a steady flow of new creative in test.

None of that needs a human every day. It needs consistency, which is exactly what software is good at. That is what AI ads management really means: not a robot that invents your campaigns, but a system that does the daily checking and adjusting on time, every day, without getting tired or distracted.

Across the accounts we manage the average lands at 4.2x, with ad spend down about a third for the same revenue. This guide explains where that difference comes from, what the AI actually does inside your Meta and Google accounts, and what still needs a person.

## What a media buyer does every day

Running paid ads for an online store is mostly routine. A good media buyer repeats the same loop every morning:

- **Read yesterday's numbers.** Spend, purchases, cost per order and return on ad spend for every campaign, ad set and ad.
- **Move the budget.** Give more to the ad sets that sold at a good cost, and less to the ones that didn't.
- **Pause the losers.** Stop ads that keep spending without bringing orders.
- **Watch for fatigue.** An ad that worked last week starts costing more as the same people see it again and again.
- **Launch new tests.** Add new images, videos and headlines so there is always something fresh to replace tired ads.

The loop is simple. The hard part is doing it carefully every single day, across dozens of ads and two or three platforms, without missing a weekend or a busy week.

## What AI ads management actually does

AI ads management takes that daily loop and runs it automatically, based on rules and targets you agree on:

1. **It reads the results continuously.** Instead of one check in the morning, performance is tracked throughout the day, on Meta (Facebook and Instagram) and Google together.
2. **It moves budget toward what sells.** Ad sets that bring orders below your target cost get more budget; ad sets above it get less. The shift is gradual, so the platforms' own learning isn't disrupted.
3. **It pauses what is dragging.** Ads that pass a spending limit without orders are stopped before they waste more money.
4. **It spots fatigue early.** When the cost per order of a winning ad starts to climb, it is flagged so a new creative can take its place.
5. **It keeps creative testing running.** New ads enter in small test budgets, and only the ones that prove themselves get scaled.
6. **It reports in plain numbers.** You see what was spent, what it brought back and what changed, without digging through Ads Manager.

None of this replaces Meta's or Google's own algorithms. It works on top of them, making the decisions a media buyer would make, but faster and more consistently. That is the core of our [AI smart ads service](/solutions/ai-smart-ads).

## Why consistency lowers your cost per order

Most wasted ad spend doesn't come from bad strategy. It comes from delay:

- An ad that stopped working on Thursday keeps spending until someone checks on Monday.
- A winning ad set stays on a small budget for days because nobody had time to scale it.
- A new product launch runs on old creative because testing fell behind.

Each of these costs a little. Together, across a month, they add up to a large share of your budget. When the checking and adjusting happen every day without fail, that waste shrinks, and the same budget brings more orders. That is where results like a lower spend for the same revenue come from: not magic, just fewer days of money going to the wrong place.

## How much do Facebook ads cost in Egypt?

This is one of the most common questions store owners ask, and the honest answer is that there is no fixed price. Meta runs an auction, so the cost of your ads depends on:

- **Your audience.** Broad audiences in Egypt are usually cheaper to reach than narrow, high-competition ones.
- **The season.** Costs rise around Ramadan, Black Friday (White Friday) and the end of the year, when many brands advertise at once.
- **Your creative.** Ads that people click and engage with get shown more cheaply than ads they scroll past.
- **Your website.** A slow site or a confusing checkout raises your cost per order, even if the cost per click is low.
- **Your goal.** Paying for reach, clicks, messages or purchases each gives a different cost.

So instead of asking "how much does a Facebook ad cost?", it is more useful to ask "how much does each order cost me, and is that profitable?" That is the number AI ads management is built to bring down. You set the daily or monthly budget yourself, and the system makes every pound of it work harder.

## Meta or Google: where should your budget go?

Both, usually, but for different jobs:

- **Meta (Facebook and Instagram)** is strong at creating demand: showing your products to people who weren't searching for them yet.
- **Google** is strong at capturing demand: reaching people who are already searching for what you sell.

The right split is different for every store and changes over time. Because AI ads management watches both platforms together, the budget can move to whichever one is bringing orders at the lowest cost that week, instead of being fixed at the start of the month.

## What still needs a person

AI handles the routine well. These parts still need human judgment:

- **Strategy and offers.** Which products to push, what discount to run and when to launch are business decisions.
- **Creative direction.** The AI can tell you which ad is winning; people still need to make the next good idea.
- **Brand and tone.** What your brand says, and doesn't say, should be decided by people.
- **Fixing the store.** If the ads bring visitors but the site doesn't convert, the fix is on the website, not in the ad account. [Speed, product pages and checkout](/solutions/shopify-optimization) matter as much as the ads themselves.

The best setup is a team that focuses on these decisions while the daily optimization runs on its own.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a big budget for AI ads management?

No. The same daily optimization works on small and large budgets. With a smaller budget, it matters even more that no money is wasted on ads that don't sell.

### Will I lose access to my ad accounts?

No. The ad accounts, pages and pixel stay yours. You keep full access, set the total budget and can see every change that was made.

### How long before I see results?

The first changes in waste usually show within the first weeks, as budget stops going to ads that don't sell. Stable results take longer, because the platforms and the tests need time to learn what works for your store.

### Does it work with Google Ads too, or only Facebook?

Both. AI ads management covers Meta (Facebook and Instagram) and Google together, so budget can move between them based on where orders cost less.

---

title: Putting an AI agent on WhatsApp without annoying your customers
excerpt: How to automate 80% of support and keep the other 20% genuinely human.
author: hams
body:
**Every message you answer late… is a customer who went somewhere else.**

A customer who messages you at 2 a.m. won't wait until morning. If they don't get a reply in seconds, they'll go to the first store that answers. A WhatsApp AI agent closes that door for good: it replies **instantly, 24 hours a day, to every message**, so you win the customer even when you're not there.

This isn't a boring menu bot that traps customers in "press 1… press 2". It's a smart assistant that understands how your customers actually write, in Egyptian Arabic, with spelling mistakes, mixing Arabic and English. It replies naturally, like your best salesperson, and it closes the sale.

And the rule that separates a bot that works from one that fails is simple: support automation fails when the bot pretends to know things it does not. It works when it answers the questions it can answer instantly, and hands over cleanly when it cannot.

---

## What is a chatbot? 🤖

A chatbot is a program that replies to messages automatically. The customer writes on WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram or your website, and the bot answers without anyone on your team typing the reply.

There are two completely different kinds:

- **Menu bots:** they show a fixed list, and if the customer writes anything outside it, they get stuck.
- **AI agents:** they understand normal language, look up the answer in your store's real data, and reply naturally.

Most of the bad experiences people have had came from the first kind. The WhatsApp AI agent we're talking about here is the second kind.

---

## The problem that costs you money every day 💸

- Lots of messages get answered late or forgotten → **lost sales**.
- Your team spends half the day answering the same repeated questions.
- Customers ask about the price or the size… and disappear.
- Messages arrive at night and wait until the morning.
- WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram each live on a different phone, and messages get lost.

In practice about four in five messages are order status, shipping and product questions. Those can be answered in under two seconds from live store data.

Examples of questions you get every day that the assistant can answer on its own:

- "Where is my order?"
- "How much is delivery to Alexandria?"
- "Is size L available?"
- "Do you have it in black?"
- "Can I pay cash on delivery?"
- "How do I return an item?"

Every one of these already has an answer in your store: the order record, the shipping rates, the stock and the return policy. Nobody on your team needs to think to answer them. They just need to look something up, and the assistant does that much faster.

**The solution?** One assistant that takes all of this off your plate and leaves your team for the things that really matter.

---

## What does a WhatsApp AI agent actually do? ✨

It doesn't just reply. It **sells, follows up and organizes**:

1. **Replies instantly, day and night** ⚡ No customer waits, and no message gets lost.
2. **Knows the order status** 📦 It reads the order from your store and tells the customer exactly where it is, with the tracking link.
3. **Answers product questions** 🛍️ Sizes, colors, materials, prices and availability, straight from your product data.
4. **Takes the order inside the chat** 🧾 The customer asks, chooses and confirms on WhatsApp, and the order is created automatically in your store.
5. **Brings back hesitant customers** 🔁 A friendly follow-up message brings back people who asked and went quiet.
6. **Recommends other products** 💡 It increases the value of each order (upsell).
7. **Organizes conversations** 🗂️ It tags them by topic, and angry or urgent customers move to the top of the list.
8. **Hands over to a person at the right moment** 🤝 With the full picture attached, so no customer is lost.

And if you have more than one WhatsApp number, they all sit in [one smart inbox](/automations/whatsapp-ai-system), so your team works from one screen instead of several phones.

---

## Why is this different from any other bot? 🎯

| Regular bot ❌ | AI agent ✅ |
|---|---|
| Fixed menus, stuck if the customer writes freely | Understands normal language and Egyptian Arabic |
| Traps the customer in buttons | Replies naturally, like a real employee |
| Old, repeated answers | Live answers from your store's data |
| Frustrates the customer | Builds trust and gets them to buy |

When it's set up well, **many customers don't realize they're talking to software** until someone from the team joins the chat.

---

## The results you'll feel 📈

- **More sales:** because you win the customer in the moment instead of losing them to someone else.
- **Less work for your team:** repeated questions answer themselves.
- **No customer gets lost:** night, day, weekends or rush hours.
- **Your brand, your voice:** you decide the tone and the rules completely.

---

## How does it work without annoying your customers? 🧠

We set it up carefully. We don't just throw it at your customers:

1. **It starts with the most repeated questions:** we review your messages and make sure the assistant masters the most important ones first.
2. **It connects to your real data:** orders, products, stock and shipping, so answers are always up to date. Order tracking works best when your [order-to-delivery flow](/blog/automate-shopify-order-to-delivery) is already automated.
3. **In your brand's style:** formal or friendly, Egyptian Arabic or English, emojis or not.
4. **With clear handover rules:** any sensitive topic goes straight to a person.
5. **It improves every week:** we review conversations and add answers for new questions.

Most importantly: **the handover to a person arrives with the full conversation**, the customer's history, what the assistant already answered, and why it handed over. The remaining fifth reaches your team with the full conversation attached, so nobody asks the customer to repeat themselves. Your team replies **once, and correctly**, without asking "how can I help you?" from the start. That's the difference between automation customers love and automation they try to escape.

---

## Is a WhatsApp AI agent right for your store? Most likely yes, if… ✅

- You get many repeated messages.
- Your customers write at night.
- You have more than one number or channel.
- Some people ask and disappear without finishing the order.

And if you still get few messages, we start small: instant replies to your top 5 questions, then expand as your store grows.

---

## Frequently asked questions 💬

### What's the difference between a WhatsApp AI agent and a regular bot?

A regular bot follows a fixed menu and gets stuck when the customer writes freely. An AI agent understands normal messages and Egyptian Arabic, looks up the answer in your store's data, and hands over to your team at the right moment.

### Does it reply in Egyptian Arabic?

Yes. It understands and replies in Egyptian Arabic and English, even messages that mix the two or have mistakes, in your brand's style.

### Will customers know they're talking to AI?

That's your decision. What matters most is that the answers are correct, and that a person is always one message away.

### Do I need the WhatsApp Business API?

Yes, and it's part of the project. We handle the whole setup.

---

## 🖤 Feel the difference from day one

Want to know how **many of your WhatsApp messages the assistant could answer today**, and how many customers it could win back that you're losing now?

**📩 [Book a free consultation](/contact)**: we'll review your most repeated questions and show you exactly what can be automated, and how much it will save you.

**Instead of working in the chat 24 hours a day… let the assistant sell, and focus on your business.**
